## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kāmajātaka* (Ja 467) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the narrative background recorded in its blurb, the Buddha spoke the story while staying at the Jetavana monastery concerning a certain brahmin, introducing verses opening with the theme "He that desires" [SuttaCentral]. In V. Fausböll's edition of the Jātaka commentary, the birth story concludes with the identification (*samodhāna*) in which the Bodhisatta is identified as the wise youth (*paṇḍitamāṇava*) who brought the brahmin out of grief [Fausböll 1887]. The title also appears in modern canonical anthologies of verse [Ānandajoti 2010].
The verses of the *Kāmajātaka* have extensive parallels and text reuse across early Buddhist and exegetical literature. SuttaCentral identifies canonical parallels in the *Kāma Sutta* of the Sutta Nipāta (Snp 4.1), the *Raṭṭhapāla Sutta* (MN 82), and the *Raṭṭhapālattheragāthā* (Thag 16.4), along with non-Pali versions in the *Śarīrārthagāthā* and the *Kāmavarga* chapter of the *Udānavarga* (extant in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese translations: T 212.2 and T 213.2) [SuttaCentral]. The text is further referenced or analyzed in exegetical works, including the *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 1), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 4, Ne 15), and the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus matches confirm this textual relationship, recording internal reuse across 10 segments with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* and 4 segments with the *Kāmasuttaniddesa* (§0.4–2.2 ↔ §11.1–13.2) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments by DharmaNexus also agree with SuttaCentral by finding matches in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga de Subaši*, alongside machine alignments with Tibetan translations of the *Saddharmānusmṛtyupasthānasūtra* and the *Pitāputrasamāgamana* [DharmaNexus].
